title: Antennae Galaxies reloaded
caption: The Antennae Galaxies, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Antennae, Antennae Galaxies, NGC 4038, NGC 4039 · constellation Corvus · about 65 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #9 on ESA/Hubble’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: Bright pink and red gas clouds surround flashes of blue star-forming regions, some partly hidden behind dark patches of dust. This is the Antennae Galaxies, NGC 4038 and NGC 4039, a colliding pair about 65 million light-years away in the constellation Corvus.

Both were once calm spirals like the Milky Way, but for the past few hundred million years they have been clashing. The encounter is violent enough to pull stars out of each galaxy into a streaming arc between them. Wider views show far-flung stars and gas stretching into long tidal tails, which give the pair its name.

The galaxies are in a starburst, a phase in which their gas is being turned into stars at a furious rate. It cannot last. Eventually the two cores will merge, and the pair will settle into retirement together as one large elliptical galaxy.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.80 x 2.78 arcminutes) and distance (65 million light years), the frame spans roughly 53,000 × 53,000 light-years. Its light set out about 65 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 and Advanced Camera for Surveys supplied visible and near-infrared observations. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
filters: 658 nm · Optical H-alpha + N II (Hubble ACS)
understand.eye: The near-infrared part of this light is invisible to the eye, and long exposures reveal far fainter gas and stars than an eye could see.

explore: Hubble had imaged the pair twice before, with WFPC2 in 1997 and with ACS in 2006. Each version improved on the last thanks to upgrades carried out during Hubble's servicing missions. This one combines Wide Field Camera 3 data with some earlier ACS observations.
alt: Two merging galaxies with bright pink and red gas clouds, blue star-forming regions and dark patches of dust.
